subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted vs current provider
messages:
From: Tom Brewer <tom.brewer@finlytics.com>

Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets from today's call

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo today. A couple of clarifications from our side after we regrouped with SRE:

- Current goals: p95 end-to-end (app → model → response) <= 450ms for single-turn chat, p99 <= 900ms. These numbers are what our product teams consider acceptable for interactive features.
- Workload: ~800 RPS at peak with expected burst concurrency up to 1.6k for short windows.
- Streaming: we stream tokens to clients; initial token latency (time-to-first-byte) is particularly sensitive — ideally <120ms p95.
- Provider: our current managed provider claims ~400ms p95 on their benchmarks but our production traces show p95 closer to ~700ms and p99 spikes above 1.2s during sustained bursts.

I'll attach the sampling of traces we pulled this morning — it shows a few consistent tail events tied to autoscaling pauses and cold-start-like behavior.

Next steps from our execs: we want a short qualification note from Redwood on whether you can reasonably hit the p95/p99 numbers above on Hosted API with our mix (320B open model, streaming enabled, auth + middleware). Also high-level guidance on throughput/concurrency limits and recommended autoscale/burst config.

Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Tom
Sr. Engineering Manager, Finlytics

Attachments: finlytics-latency-traces-0509.zip (log snippets, 20KB)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets from today's call

Hi Tom —

Really appreciate the detailed notes and the trace bundle. Quick recap and initial qualification notes from our side:

1) Short answer: we believe Redwood Hosted can meet your p95/p99 targets in most steady-state scenarios and offer more consistent tails versus what you described seeing with your current provider. That said, meeting p95 <= 450ms and p99 <= 900ms for streaming workloads depends on a few inputs (model size/config, effective batching, and network placement).

2) Key assumptions we used for this qualification:
   - Model: 320B open model (quantized to 4-bit equivalent with KV cache).
   - Payload: average prompt length 120 tokens, response length 80 tokens.
   - Network: requests originate from US-west region (we recommend colocating Redwood endpoints in the same region).

3) Preliminary baseline we can reliably achieve on Hosted (subject to an official perf run / PoC):
   - p95 end-to-end: ~350-420ms (single-turn, TTFB ~90-120ms)
   - p99 end-to-end: ~700-850ms (depends on burst handling)
   - Sustained throughput per instance: ~250–350 RPS (model and instance type dependent)
   - Burst capacity: we recommend reserved burst pools + autoscale policies to cover short 2x bursts; with dedicated burst configured, effective peak handling up to 1.5–2x sustained per pool.

4) Streaming specifics: Redwood's streaming path is optimized to pipeline token generation and network I/O — TTFB p95 in our Hosted runs is typically ~80–120ms for the model family you described. The tail at p99 is often influenced by upstream network variability and throttling in customer middleware.

5) Risks and follow-ups:
   - Cold starts: unlikely on Hosted if you pin warm pools, but container-level restarts can cause outliers — we'll outline keep-alive recommendations.
   - Autoscale tuning: we'll provide recommended target CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth thresholds.
   - Perf run: next step is to schedule a short PoC/perf run using your sample traces and production-like concurrency. That will give definitive p95/p99 numbers and trace-level breakdowns.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-slo-matrix.pdf (attached: high-level SLO matrix and recommended autoscale settings)

Action items:
- We'll run a short PoC (2–4 hours) using your trace sample and a staging key — can we book the run for Wednesday (5/12) afternoon PT?
- Marissa will own the tuning/benchmarks; Aditya will validate the streaming path and provide config snippets for SDKs.

Looping Marissa and Aditya for scheduling and technical notes.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
